finding.claim: Xxh32::update truncates input.len() to u32 and adds it to mem_size with wrapping arithmetic in release builds. For a slice whose length is a multiple of 2^32 (e.g. exactly 4 GiB), the check passes and the full untruncated slice is copied into the 16-byte mem buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write.
finding.source: src/xxh32.rs:102 Xxh32::update(&mut self, input: &[u8]) - caller-supplied slice; attacker controls bytes and, when passing a >=4 GiB buffer, its length
finding.sink: src/utils.rs:48 ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(src, self.ptr.add(self.offset), len) reached via src/xxh32.rs:108-111 Buffer::copy_from_slice on the 16-byte self.mem field

trace.note: guard (mem_size + input.len() as u32) < 16; input.len()=2^32 truncates to 0 so guard is true
debug_assert only; compiled out in release
copy_nonoverlapping writes len bytes into 16-byte field

finding.guards_checked: Guard at xxh32.rs:106 is the only size check and it uses truncated u32 arithmetic. utils.rs:45 is debug_assert only (no release check).
